passages.title: The new gym
passages.text:
Gareth: How's the new gym, Olivia?
Olivia: The machines are all brand new, and it's only five minutes from my flat.
Gareth: Sounds perfect.
Olivia: It would be, but I can only go after work, and that's when everyone else goes. I usually have to wait ages to use anything. I might start going early in the morning instead.

passages.title: A running app
passages.text:
Woman: You've been out running every day this week, Max!
Max: It's this app. It gives you points for every kilometre, and you can see how your friends are doing. I'm trying to beat Lewis.
Woman: I thought you hated running.
Max: I did! But now it's like a game. And it was free, so you can't complain.

passages.title: Getting enough sleep
passages.text:
Fiona: I read that we should all sleep eight hours a night. I'm lucky if I get six.
Dominic: Me too. I always look at my phone in bed, and then I'm awake for ages.
Fiona: Same here. I really think the screen keeps you awake. I'm going to leave mine in the kitchen.
Dominic: Good idea. Mind you, I went swimming yesterday and I still couldn't sleep.
Fiona: Really? Swimming always makes me sleep like a baby.

passages.title: Starting yoga
passages.text:
Marcus: Since when do you do yoga, Holly?
Holly: Since January. My sister's been trying to get me to go with her for years, but I always said no.
Marcus: So what changed your mind?
Holly: Exams, really. I was so stressed I couldn't think properly. Someone told me yoga helps you relax, so I tried it. And it works. I feel much calmer now. My sister's really happy I'm there, of course!

passages.title: Cycling to work
passages.text:
Kirsty: Are you still cycling to work, Ian?
Ian: Every day. I thought it would take much longer than the car, but with all the traffic in the mornings, I actually get there ten minutes earlier.
Kirsty: Isn't it dangerous, though, on those busy roads?
Ian: There's a cycle path most of the way now, so I feel quite safe. And I'm not tired at all. I've got more energy than before.

passages.title: A month without sugar
passages.text:
Ruth: So, how's the no-sugar month going, Pete?
Pete: Well, I was sure I'd be desperate for chocolate after a couple of days. But honestly, I hardly think about it.
Ruth: Really? I'd find it impossible.
Pete: So did I! I haven't lost any weight yet, but that wasn't really why I did it. I just wanted to have more energy.

questions.question: You will hear two friends talking about a gym. What problem does Olivia have with it?
options: a) It is a long way from her home.
b) It is too busy when she can go.
c) The equipment is quite old.
questions.explanation: Olivia says "I can only go after work, and that's when everyone else goes. I usually have to wait ages". The gym is "only five minutes from my flat" and the machines are "brand new".

questions.question: You will hear a boy talking to his mother about a running app. What does he think of the app?
options: a) It was too expensive to download.
b) It has made running more fun.
c) It makes running too hard.
questions.explanation: Max says he hated running, "But now it's like a game", and he is "trying to beat Lewis". The app "was free", and nothing suggests it makes running too hard.

questions.question: You will hear two friends talking about sleep. What do they agree about?
options: a) Using a phone in bed stops you sleeping.
b) Eight hours of sleep is too much.
c) Doing exercise during the day helps you sleep.
questions.explanation: Dominic looks at his phone in bed "and then I'm awake for ages", and Fiona says "Same here. I really think the screen keeps you awake." They disagree about exercise: swimming didn't help Dominic, but it helps Fiona.

questions.question: You will hear a girl telling a friend about yoga. Why did she start doing it?
options: a) Because her sister persuaded her
b) To make some new friends
questions.explanation: Holly says "Exams, really. I was so stressed I couldn't think properly", and she tried yoga because it "helps you relax". Her sister asked her "for years", "but I always said no", so that wasn't the reason.

questions.question: You will hear two friends talking about cycling to work. What is Ian's opinion of it?
options: a) It is dangerous on the busy roads in town.
b) It makes him feel tired.
c) It is quicker than driving.
questions.explanation: Ian says "with all the traffic in the mornings, I actually get there ten minutes earlier" than by car. It is Kirsty who thinks it is dangerous; Ian feels "quite safe" and is "not tired at all".

questions.question: You will hear a man talking about giving up sugar. How does he feel about it now?
options: a) He is surprised it has been so easy.
b) He is upset that he hasn't lost weight.
c) He misses sweet food a lot.
questions.explanation: Pete "was sure I'd be desperate for chocolate", "But honestly, I hardly think about it." He hasn't lost weight, but "that wasn't really why I did it", so he is not upset about it.
